title: 5.4.6 Plain English to Pseudocode: A Method That Calls a Method
description: Turn five plain-English steps into pseudocode: one decision, two calls to other methods, and a step that runs either way.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([takeDamage amount starts]) --> B[health = health - amount]
  B --> C{health <= 0}
  C -- yes --> D[[this.die]]
  C -- no --> E[[this.flashRed]]
  D --> E
  E --> F([back to the caller])
planChart.caption: takeDamage: the die call sits on one branch, and both branches reach flashRed.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** The enemy is hit for some amount of damage.

**2.** Take that amount off the enemy's health.

**3.** If the health is now zero or less, the enemy dies.

**4.** Either way, the enemy flashes red to show it was hit.

**5.** Then control goes back to whoever hit it.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the five steps.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Use SET for a change, IF and END IF for the decision, and CALL for the two other methods (`die` and `flashRed`). Each keyword looks like this:

- `SET health TO health - amount` (a change)
- `IF health <= 0` ... `END IF` (the decision; indent what is inside it)
- `CALL die` (call another method; you may write `CALL this.die` as the chart does)

Number every line, including the indented one and END IF. The chart shows the shape.
hints: A step that happens "either way" is not inside the IF. It comes after END IF.
Write a call as one line: `CALL die`. Do not write what die does.

requirements.title: Five numbered steps in a row
requirements.description: Number every step 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least five lines that start with a number, one after another, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: Subtract the damage from health first
requirements.description: A step like `SET health TO health - amount`, before the decision.
requirements.hint: Write the change as SET health TO health - amount, and put it before the IF.

requirements.title: One decision that asks if health is zero or less
requirements.description: Exactly one IF, written against health and zero, closed with END IF.
requirements.hint: Use one IF that asks if health is zero or less (health <= 0), and close it with END IF. If you have two IFs, join them into one.

requirements.title: CALL die happens only inside the decision
requirements.description: The CALL die line sits between IF and END IF.
requirements.hint: The enemy only dies when health is 0 or less, so CALL die goes between IF and END IF.

requirements.title: CALL flashRed happens after END IF, either way
requirements.description: The flash runs whether or not the enemy died, so it comes after END IF.
requirements.hint: Step 4 says "either way". A step that runs either way is not inside the decision: put CALL flashRed after END IF.

requirements.title: Exactly two calls
requirements.description: One CALL line for die and one for flashRed.
requirements.hint: You need exactly two CALL lines, one for die and one for flashRed. What die does belongs inside die, not here.
